newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rates seen easing if money market stablises.
newsitem.headline: Thai rates seen easing if money market stablises.

text.p: Thai banks are expected to cut interest rates in the next few weeks if the money market situation regained its posture and the overnight interbank rate returned to normal, a senior banker said on Thursday.

Olarn Chaiprawat, Thai Bankers Association president, told reporters if currency market volatility remained subdued and the central bank did not have to intervene, the interbank rate should stay at the normal 10- to 12-percent levels seen this week.

"If next week, the interbank rate stayed this way and the situation in the money market is normal, commercial banks could reduce their interest rates in the next three to four weeks," said Olarn, who is also president of Siam Commercial Bank Plc.
"But the cut will depend on individual banks' situation," Olarn said.
He said some banks might increase deposit rates to maintain their market share, but that would not be a long-term trend and would merely reflect short-term needs.
Olarn also welcomed Bank of Thailand data released on Thursday, particularly the smaller current account deficit.
December's current account deficit was 19.1 billion baht, the central bank said

The Thai economy has moved out of its high current account deficit crisis," he said, referring to its peak last April when the account showed a 49.6 billion baht ($1.9 billion) monthly deficit. -- Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642 ($ = 25.87 Thai Baht)
